entities.name: Fibromyalgia
observations: Taiwanese population-based cohorts found higher subsequent coronary heart disease incidence among patients with fibromyalgia.
Fibromyalgia was defined in the exact-title cohort as treatment at least monthly for 3 consecutive months.

entities.name: Coronary heart disease
observations: In PMID 25436616, the outcome was a composite of percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting.
In PMID 26366998, incident coronary heart disease was assessed over a mean 8.86±2.68 years.

entities.name: PMID:25436616
observations: Taiwan Longitudinal Health Insurance Database cohort study reported adjusted HR 2.11 for CHD events in fibromyalgia versus comparison participants (95% CI 1.46–3.05; P<0.001).
The study used propensity-score adjustment; cohort size, follow-up duration, and individual covariates were unavailable in the retrieved record.

entities.name: PMID:26366998
observations: Taiwanese cohort included 61,612 incident fibromyalgia patients and 184,834 matched controls, followed through 2011 for mean 8.86±2.68 years.

Incident CHD was higher with fibromyalgia: adjusted HR 1.47 (95% CI 1.43–1.51); incidence-rate ratio 1.64 (95% CI 1.61–1.68). Covariates included demographics, socioeconomic factors, cardiovascular comorbidities, depression, and anxiety.

entities.name: Fibromyalgia-CHD association
observations: Two directly relevant Taiwanese population-based cohorts were directionally concordant, reporting adjusted HRs of 2.11 and 1.47 for CHD outcomes.
These observational findings support an association with incident CHD but do not establish that fibromyalgia causes CHD.
No directly relevant null or protective cohort finding was identified in the retrieved evidence.
